root_cause.text: The `crypto/algif_aead` request path was incorrectly converted to an in-place TX/RX scatterlist handling model, even though the source and destination buffers come from different mappings, which made the AAD-copy/in-place complexity unnecessary and faulty.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message says it “Revert[s] to operating out-of-place” and that “There is no benefit in operating in-place in algif_aead since the source and destination come from different mappings,” while the diff removes the in-place encryption/decryption logic, the offset-based `af_alg_count_tsgl()`/`af_alg_pull_tsgl()` handling, and switches back to directly copying the associated data.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `crypto/algif_aead` request path incorrectly tried to support in-place AEAD processing by copying AAD/data between the TX and RX scatterlists and using offset-aware TX-SGL accounting, but the source and destination buffers come from different mappings, so this complex in-place handling could misbuild or mis-reassign scatterlist entries and corrupt request state.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch explicitly removes the offset-based `af_alg_count_tsgl()`/`af_alg_pull_tsgl()` logic and the in-place encryption/decryption branches in `_aead_recvmsg()`, replacing them with a simple out-of-place flow that creates a per-request TX SGL, copies only the associated data directly, and passes the full TX SGL to `aead_request_set_crypt()`.

root_cause_review.feedback: The evidence is mostly consistent with the patch, but the proposed root cause is too speculative and not grounded in the CVE/commit text. The CVE/commit say the issue is simply that in-place operation in `algif_aead` provides no benefit because source and destination come from different mappings, so the code should revert to out-of-place handling and just copy associated data. The root cause instead claims scatterlist entries could be “misbuilt or mis-reassigned” and “corrupt request state,” which is not stated or demonstrated by the patch. It also overfocuses on TX/RX mapping mismatch in a way that goes beyond the documented rationale.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify `af_alg_count_tsgl` by removing the unused offset parameter and documenting that counting always starts at the beginning of the SGL.
intent_record.what: The function `af_alg_count_tsgl` had its prototype changed from `unsigned int af_alg_count_tsgl(struct sock *sk, size_t bytes, size_t offset)` to `unsigned int af_alg_count_tsgl(struct sock *sk, size_t bytes)`, removing the `offset` parameter. The accompanying kernel-doc comment was updated to remove references to counting from an offset and to describe only counting from the beginning of the SGL to `bytes`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function can no longer be called with a starting offset, so counting TX scatter-gather list entries is now always performed from the beginning of the list up to the requested byte count. This simplifies the API and removes offset-based behavior from this helper.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify scatterlist counting to use full segment lengths and return as soon as the requested byte count is covered.
intent_record.what: In `af_alg_count_tsgl()`, the per-scatterlist iteration logic was simplified: the code no longer adjusts for `offset`, no longer computes `bytes_count`, and no longer skips entries based on `offset >= sg[i].length`. Instead, it now increments `sgl_count` for every entry visited, returns immediately if `sg[i].length >= bytes`, and otherwise subtracts the full segment length from `bytes`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now counts scatterlist elements using only the remaining byte budget and each element's full length, rather than accounting for an intra-element offset. This changes how many SG entries are reported as needed for a given byte request and may cause the count to include entries that were previously skipped or to stop earlier based on the raw segment length.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the `dst_offset` parameter from `af_alg_pull_tsgl` and simplify its documentation to match the reduced API.
intent_record.what: The function declaration and definition of `af_alg_pull_tsgl` were changed to remove the `dst_offset` parameter. The accompanying kernel-doc comments were updated to delete all references to `dst_offset` and to simplify the description of how reassignment to `dst` works.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers can no longer specify an offset within the destination scatterlist when pulling TX SGL buffers. The function now only supports either releasing the buffers or reassigning them starting from the beginning of `dst`, which simplifies the API and removes offset-based behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify destination scatterlist page assignment in af_alg_pull_tsgl() by removing incorrect dst_offset-based trimming logic.
intent_record.what: Inside af_alg_pull_tsgl(), the conditional logic that handled dst_offset when copying a page into the destination scatterlist was removed. Instead of either discarding the page portion before the offset or assigning a shortened page with an adjusted offset, the code now always gets a reference to the page and calls sg_set_page(dst + j, page, plen, sg[i].offset), then increments j.
intent_record.how: At runtime, every page selected for dst is now added to the destination scatterlist with the full plen length and the original page offset, regardless of dst_offset. This changes how buffered data is mapped into the destination list and removes the previous offset-based trimming behavior, which can alter how much of each page is exposed to later processing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary skcipher header include to reduce compile-time dependencies.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `#include <crypto/skcipher.h>` header from the source file, leaving the other include directives unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes compilation dependencies by no longer pulling in the skcipher API declarations from this file; runtime behavior is unaffected unless the removed include was only needed for unused declarations, in which case it simply reduces coupling and potential compile-time dependencies.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove obsolete local variable declarations from `_aead_recvmsg()`.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in `_aead_recvmsg()` was changed from `unsigned int i, as = crypto_aead_authsize(tfm);` to `unsigned int as = crypto_aead_authsize(tfm);`, removing the unused `i` declaration. The declaration `struct af_alg_tsgl *tsgl, *tmp;` was also removed.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter the function’s runtime logic; it only removes variables that are no longer needed in this scope, reducing unused declarations and avoiding compiler warnings.

intent_record.intent_summary: Create and use a per-request TX scatterlist snapshot for AEAD receive processing instead of relying on the global TX SGL search.
intent_record.what: The code removes the loop that searched the global TX scatterlist (`ctx->tsgl_list`) for the first valid source entry and the associated `-EFAULT` path when `processed` was nonzero but no entry was found. In its place, it computes `areq->tsgl_entries` with `af_alg_count_tsgl(sk, processed)`, forces it to at least 1, allocates a per-request scatterlist buffer with `sock_kmalloc(...)`, returns `-ENOMEM` on allocation failure, initializes the new table with `sg_init_table(...)`, populates it via `af_alg_pull_tsgl(sk, processed, areq->tsgl)`, and assigns `tsgl_src = areq->tsgl`. A comment was added describing the creation of a per-request TX SGL tracking the global TX SGL entries.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the request now gets its own scatterlist copy instead of borrowing the first usable entry from the shared TX list. This makes the request processing operate on a stable per-request SGL snapshot, avoiding dependence on walking the global list at this point and changing the failure mode from missing source data to memory allocation failure if the per-request SGL cannot be created.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify AEAD receive handling by removing special-case in-place scatterlist manipulation and using a unified source setup for the crypto request.
intent_record.what: The code removed the entire ctx->enc conditional block that previously handled encryption and decryption differently with separate scatter-gather list copying, tag extraction, and chaining logic. In its place, it now unconditionally copies ctx->aead_assoclen bytes from tsgl_src into rsgl_src, and the aead_request_set_crypt() call was changed to pass tsgl_src as the source scatterlist instead of rsgl_src.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the AEAD receive path no longer builds distinct in-place buffer layouts for encrypt versus decrypt. Instead, it always copies only the associated-data portion into the RX scatterlist and uses the original TX scatterlist as the crypto source, which changes how the cipher sees input buffers and simplifies the data path for the AEAD request setup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the AEAD socket destructor to call `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` with the updated argument list.
intent_record.what: In `aead_sock_destruct()`, the call to `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` was changed from passing four arguments (`sk, ctx->used, NULL, 0`) to passing three arguments (`sk, ctx->used, NULL`), removing the explicit zero length argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this updates the destructor to use the revised `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` interface. Behaviorally, it still pulls and releases the AEAD scatterlist state during socket teardown, but now matches the function's current parameter contract so destruction can proceed correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update `_skcipher_recvmsg()` to use the corrected `af_alg_count_tsgl()` call signature when calculating TX SGL entries.
intent_record.what: The call to `af_alg_count_tsgl()` in `_skcipher_recvmsg()` was changed from passing three arguments (`sk, len, 0`) to passing two arguments (`sk, len`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the request now derives `tsgl_entries` using the updated `af_alg_count_tsgl()` interface, which no longer takes the extra zero argument; this aligns the caller with the current function signature and ensures the TX scatter-gather list entry count is computed as intended.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update `_skcipher_recvmsg()` to use the corrected `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` call signature.
intent_record.what: The call to `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` in `_skcipher_recvmsg()` was changed from passing four arguments (`sk, len, areq->tsgl, 0`) to passing three arguments (`sk, len, areq->tsgl`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes how the scatter-gather list is populated for the skcipher receive path by using the updated `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` interface, which no longer takes the final zero argument and therefore affects how the input data is pulled into the request.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the skcipher socket destructor to call `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` with the correct argument list.
intent_record.what: The call to `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` in `skcipher_sock_destruct()` was changed from passing four arguments (`sk`, `ctx->used`, `NULL`, `0`) to passing three arguments (`sk`, `ctx->used`, `NULL`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the destructor now uses the updated `af_alg_pull_tsgl()` interface, removing the extra zero argument. This affects only the function invocation signature and ensures the socket teardown path matches the current helper API.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify the AF_ALG scatterlist helper interfaces by removing now-unneeded parameters.
intent_record.what: The declarations of af_alg_count_tsgl() and af_alg_pull_tsgl() were changed to remove parameters: af_alg_count_tsgl() no longer takes a size_t offset argument, and af_alg_pull_tsgl() no longer takes a struct scatterlist *dst_offset argument.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers of these helpers will now use simpler interfaces that only pass the total byte count or destination scatterlist, implying the removed arguments are no longer needed for the underlying logic and that the helpers' behavior is now driven by fewer inputs.

candidates.content: /* Use the RX SGL as source (and destination) for crypto op. */
candidates.rationale: This reflects the incorrect in-place TX/RX model at the heart of the bug: the AEAD path was treating RX as both source and destination even though TX and RX buffers are from different mappings.
This sets the crypto request source to the RX scatterlist, embodying the mistaken in-place handling assumption that the receive buffer can serve as the operation source/destination.
This is a direct manifestation of the faulty in-place conversion: data is copied into RX as if TX/RX were a unified buffer arrangement, which is unnecessary and error-prone when the mappings differ.

This statement is part of the same incorrect receive-side in-place manipulation for decryption, copying from TX into RX to simulate in-place processing despite separate source and destination buffers.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assigns the AEAD crypto request source directly to the receive scatterlist, reflecting the incorrect in-place TX/RX assumption even though the send and receive buffers are separately mapped.
This copies decrypted output into the receive scatterlist as part of the flawed in-place handling model, despite the source and destination buffers not sharing a single mapping.
This is the same faulty receive-side scatterlist copying pattern for the AEAD request path, treating RX as if it were the in-place destination for TX data.
